summary:
AFTERLIGHT is an interactive 3D storytelling experience created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, "Abandoned but Not Forgotten".

We built AFTERLIGHT to make learning about the objects left behind on the Moon and Mars more fun and engaging. Instead of reading long, text-heavy articles, users can listen to narrated stories, explore interactive 3D models of real space equipment, and learn about the missions behind them.

Our goal is to highlight the forgotten tools and machines that helped explore space. Even though these objects were left behind, they remain part of space exploration history. We believe their stories deserve to be told, and the missions behind them should never be forgotten.
details:
AFTERLIGHT is a chapter-based interactive storytelling website that helps people discover the objects left behind by space exploration missions on the Moon and Mars. Users start at a hero section and navigate through different chapters, with each chapter focusing on a specific object and the mission behind it.

Each chapter explains what the object was used for, its role in the mission, and why it was left behind. Instead of relying on long articles and static images, users can explore interactive 3D models, rotate them, zoom in, and listen to narrated stories. They can also pause and replay the narration at any time.

The main benefit of AFTERLIGHT is that it makes learning about space exploration more interesting and accessible. It helps users understand the history and purpose of these objects while creating a stronger connection with them through interaction and storytelling. The project is intended for students, teachers, space enthusiasts, and anyone curious about space. Our goal is to bring attention to these forgotten objects and make sure the missions and achievements behind them are not forgotten.

We developed AFTERLIGHT using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, with Three.js for displaying and handling the interactive 3D models and GSAP for animations and smooth transitions throughout the website. We downloaded existing models from NASA's 3D resources and used information from NASA and the National Space Science Data Center (NSSDC) for our content. ElevenLabs was used to create the voice narration.

What makes AFTERLIGHT creative is the way it combines storytelling, voice narration, animations, and interactive 3D models to turn traditional educational content into an experience people can actively take part in. Rather than simply reading about an object, users can explore it while hearing its story.

Throughout development, our team focused on keeping scientific information easy to understand, making the experience visually engaging, using accurate information and models, and creating a website that is accessible and easy to navigate.
